newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mint zinc tender sees wide range of premiums.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mint zinc tender sees wide range of premiums.

text.p: Premiums on metal offered in U.S. Mint zinc tender announced Jan 23 were wide, with the lower end of the range below spot market levels, traders said.
The Mint sought 2,964 tonnes of special high grade metal, and is due to announce the awards soon.
Only four participants offered metal, Trademet, Hochschild Partners, Val, and Ore & Chemical, at premiums ranging from 4.95 cents per lb over LME cash to 6.49 cents.

The lower end was offered by Val, though only on 200 tonnes for the La Salle Rolling Mills in Illinois, with the higher premiums on metal for Alltrista Zinc Division, Tennessee, the two locations the Mint takes delivery of metal.

Although a premium of below 5.00 cents was offered, traders and merchants insisted that other spot deals were still easily commanding 5.5 cents per lb or higher because the U.S. physical market remained relatively tight.
Premiums on the bulk of the Mint tender material were in line or above spot levels.
"People don't have a lot of zinc to offer, so why give metal away to the Mint," a producer agent said.

Dealers said zinc deliveries were going full tilt, but following the recent run-up in zinc prices on LME, fresh business and pricing of existing orders were being put on hold by some consumers who were crossing their fingers for a downward price correction.
"We will probably have a correction in all the metals as the copper spreads come in," a trader said. "But if there is a true deficit of zinc out there, then the price will start moving up again."
